notes:
Angle Measurement

  • $180^\circ = \pi$ radians; $1^\circ = \pi/180$ rad. Arc length $s = r\theta$ ($\theta$ in radians).

Trigonometric identities

  • $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$; $1+\tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta$; $1+\cot^2\theta = \text{cosec}^2\theta$.
  • Range: $-1 \le \sin\theta, \cos\theta \le 1$; $\sec\theta, \text{cosec}\theta \in (-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)$; $\tan\theta,\cot\theta \in \mathbb{R}$.

Sum, difference & multiple angle formulas

  • $\sin(A\pm B) = \sin A\cos B \pm \cos A\sin B$; $\cos(A\pm B) = \cos A\cos B \mp \sin A\sin B$.
  • $\tan(A\pm B) = \dfrac{\tan A \pm \tan B}{1 \mp \tan A\tan B}$.
  • $\sin 2A = 2\sin A\cos A$; $\cos 2A = \cos^2A - \sin^2A = 1-2\sin^2A = 2\cos^2A-1$; $\tan 2A = \dfrac{2\tan A}{1-\tan^2A}$.
  • $\sin 3A = 3\sin A - 4\sin^3A$; $\cos 3A = 4\cos^3A - 3\cos A$.

Transformation formulas

  • $\sin C + \sin D = 2\sin\dfrac{C+D}{2}\cos\dfrac{C-D}{2}$; $\cos C + \cos D = 2\cos\dfrac{C+D}{2}\cos\dfrac{C-D}{2}$; $\cos C - \cos D = -2\sin\dfrac{C+D}{2}\sin\dfrac{C-D}{2}$.
  • $2\sin A\cos B = \sin(A+B)+\sin(A-B)$; $2\cos A\cos B = \cos(A+B)+\cos(A-B)$.

General solutions

  • $\sin\theta = \sin\alpha \Rightarrow \theta = n\pi + (-1)^n\alpha$.
  • $\cos\theta = \cos\alpha \Rightarrow \theta = 2n\pi \pm \alpha$.
  • $\tan\theta = \tan\alpha \Rightarrow \theta = n\pi + \alpha$, $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

Exam tip

KCET usually asks 2–3 questions from this chapter — mostly on compound/multiple angle identities, general solutions of trig equations, and quadrant sign rules. Memorise the standard-angle table and $\sin2A,\cos2A$ forms cold; they are the fastest-solving questions in the paper.

questions.q: If $\cos\theta = -\dfrac12$ and $\theta$ lies in the third quadrant, then $\theta$ equals (principal value in $[0,2\pi)$)

questions.q: If $\sin x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$ and $x$ is in the first quadrant, the value of $\sin 2x$ is
questions.explanation: $x = \pi/4$ (since $\sin x = 1/\sqrt2$ in QI), so $\sin2x = \sin(\pi/2) = 1$.

questions.q: The value of $\cos 2\theta$ in terms of $\tan\theta$ is
questions.explanation: Dividing $\cos2\theta = \cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta$ by $\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta=1$ and dividing num/denom by $\cos^2\theta$ gives $\cos2\theta = \dfrac{1-\tan^2\theta}{1+\tan^2\theta}$.

questions.q: If $A + B = 45^\circ$, the value of $(1+\tan A)(1+\tan B)$ is
questions.explanation: $\tan(A+B)=1 \Rightarrow \dfrac{\tan A+\tan B}{1-\tan A\tan B}=1 \Rightarrow \tan A+\tan B = 1-\tan A\tan B$. Expanding $(1+\tan A)(1+\tan B) = 1+\tan A+\tan B+\tan A\tan B = 1+(1-\tan A\tan B)+\tan A\tan B = 2$.
$-1200^\circ + 4\times360^\circ = 240^\circ$, and $\sin(-1200^\circ) = \sin240^\circ = -\sin60^\circ = -\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

questions.q: If $\cot\theta = \dfrac{4}{3}$ and $\theta$ lies in the first quadrant, the value of $\text{cosec}\,\theta$ is
questions.explanation: $1+\cot^2\theta = \text{cosec}^2\theta = 1+\dfrac{16}{9} = \dfrac{25}{9} \Rightarrow \text{cosec}\,\theta = \dfrac{5}{3}$ (positive in QI).

questions.q: The number of solutions of $\cos\theta = 0$ in $[0, 2\pi]$ is
questions.explanation: $\cos\theta = 0$ at $\theta = \pi/2$ and $3\pi/2$ within $[0,2\pi]$ — exactly 2 solutions.

questions.q: If $\sin A = \dfrac35$ (A acute) and $\cos B = \dfrac{5}{13}$ (B acute), the value of $\sin(A+B)$ is
questions.explanation: $\cos A = 4/5$, $\sin B = 12/13$. $\sin(A+B) = \sin A\cos B+\cos A\sin B = \dfrac{3}{5}\cdot\dfrac{5}{13}+\dfrac{4}{5}\cdot\dfrac{12}{13} = \dfrac{15+48}{65} = \dfrac{63}{65}$.
Using $\tan2\theta$ formula with $\theta=\pi/8$: $\tan(\pi/4)=1=\dfrac{2t}{1-t^2}$ where $t=\tan(\pi/8)$. Solving $t^2+2t-1=0 \Rightarrow t = -1+\sqrt2$ (taking positive root since $\pi/8$ is in QI).
$\sin50^\circ - \sin70^\circ = -2\cos60^\circ\sin10^\circ = -2(1/2)\sin10^\circ = -\sin10^\circ$. Adding $\sin10^\circ$ gives $0$.

questions.q: The period of the function $f(x) = \sin\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$ is
questions.explanation: Period of $\sin(kx)$ is $2\pi/k$; here $k=1/2$, so period $= 2\pi/(1/2) = 4\pi$.

questions.q: Which of the following is a solution of $2\cos^2\theta + 3\sin\theta = 0$?
questions.explanation: $2(1-\sin^2\theta)+3\sin\theta=0 \Rightarrow -2\sin^2\theta+3\sin\theta+2=0 \Rightarrow 2\sin^2\theta-3\sin\theta-2=0 \Rightarrow (2\sin\theta+1)(\sin\theta-2)=0$. Since $\sin\theta\ne2$, $\sin\theta=-1/2$, satisfied by $\theta=7\pi/6$ (check: $\sin(7\pi/6)=-1/2$).

questions.q: The degree measure of $\dfrac{7\pi}{6}$ radians is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{7\pi}{6} \times \dfrac{180^\circ}{\pi} = 7 \times 30^\circ = 210^\circ$.

questions.q: In the third quadrant, which of the following trigonometric ratios is positive?
questions.explanation: In the third quadrant, only $\tan\theta$ and $\cot\theta$ are positive; sine, cosine and their reciprocals are negative.
$\cos15^\circ = \cos(45^\circ-30^\circ) = \cos45^\circ\cos30^\circ+\sin45^\circ\sin30^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4}$.
This is the standard angle-difference formula for sine.
Since $\tan$ has period $\pi$ and $\tan\frac{\pi}{4}=1$, the general solution is $\theta = n\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, $n\in\mathbb Z$.
The standard general solution of $\cos\theta=\cos\alpha$ is $\theta = 2n\pi \pm \alpha$, $n\in\mathbb Z$.

questions.q: The domain of $\tan x$ excludes values of the form
questions.explanation: $\tan x = \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}$ is undefined where $\cos x = 0$, i.e. at $x = (2n+1)\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
Cosine takes all values from $-1$ to $1$, inclusive.
$\cos60^\circ = \dfrac12$, so $\sec60^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\cos60^\circ} = 2$.
$\dfrac{3\pi}{4} = 135^\circ$ lies in the second quadrant, where $\cot$ is negative; $\cot135^\circ = -\cot45^\circ = -1$.
The maximum value of $a\sin\theta+b\cos\theta$ is $\sqrt{a^2+b^2} = \sqrt{9+16} = 5$.
Sine is positive in the second quadrant, so $\sin(\pi-\theta) = \sin\theta$.
Cosine is negative in the third quadrant, so $\cos(\pi+\theta) = -\cos\theta$.
Cosine is an even function, so $\cos(-60^\circ) = \cos60^\circ = \dfrac12$.
For $y = a\sin(bx)$, the amplitude is $|a|$, which here is 3.

questions.q: The number of solutions of $\sin\theta = \cos\theta$ in $[0, 2\pi]$ is
questions.explanation: $\sin\theta=\cos\theta \Rightarrow \tan\theta=1$, giving $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ and $\dfrac{5\pi}{4}$ in $[0,2\pi]$ — 2 solutions.

questions.q: If $A+B+C = \pi$ (angles of a triangle), then $\tan A + \tan B + \tan C$ equals
questions.explanation: For angles of a triangle, $\tan A+\tan B+\tan C = \tan A\tan B\tan C$, a standard identity.
Since $A+B = \pi - C$, $\sin(A+B) = \sin(\pi-C) = \sin C$.
$\tan x$ repeats every $\pi$ radians, unlike $\sin x$ and $\cos x$ which have period $2\pi$.
$\sin18^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt5-1}{4}$ is a standard special value derived from the geometry of a regular pentagon.
